height_other: Activity was visible shortly after nautical twilight, formed by one large diffuse band to the south and arcing aurora overhead, stretching from east to west. Around 2230-2300 aurora activity exploded, starting from overhead. The aurora became very bright, stretching down from zenith over the course of 5 minutes generating large, dynamic curtains of aurora with easily detectable colors of red, green, pink, and purple to the unaided eye. This intense period of activity was roughly maintained for approximately 45 minutes until the intensity would begin to wane. After midnight, the activity would begin to concentrate across more of the northern hemisphere of the sky and be primarily made up of 10-20 min flares of arc aurora and widespread, constant diffuse and patchy aurora. Color was visible periodically with flares. Diffuse and patchy aurora was maintaining once observation ceased around 330.
activities_other: Aurora was very active with significant blurring occurring in 6 sec exposures. Most aggressive motion occurred later in the night with the diffuse and patchy aurora. 12:52 AM 3/11/2024 - Invercargill.
I went out around 22:00 to see if there was any colour as this was the first night in some time we had clear sky. It was extremely cold last night, I was rugged up like it was mid-winter, the wind chill was serious. I didn’t know if I would get anything or not. The first sign of colour and rays was around 22:30. The activity started building low on the horizon, around 12:45 am (3/11/2024) the real activity started, by 12:47 am the rays had started properly and it was all on until 01:03 am, from then it slowly reduced intensity, getting quieter as the night wore on. The main activity I captured was only a little over 15 minutes, before it started a slow decline. Putting up with the cold and the wait were well worth it. Finally heading home at 01:30 AM as the clouds were rolling in again and the Aurora was weak.
